title: American Beech Tissue Collection for DNA
author: Michelle Neitzey

steps.title: Gather required materials
steps.instruction: Collect all supplies before field work: zip‑lock bags with silica gel packets, sample ID cards, tea bags, reusable mailer, smartphone with GPS and TreeSnap app installed, pen or pencil, fabric measuring tape, cutting shears or knife, and alcohol or bleach for decontamination. For Canadian collections, have the APHIS Letter of No Permit (if required).

steps.title: Select appropriate collection site
steps.instruction: Choose a site where you have permission to collect (obtain permit for managed lands or owner consent for private lands), ensure trees are of wild provenance (avoid planted roadside trees), and locate the site at least 8 km (5 mi) from any previously collected sample.

steps.title: Identify and measure target tree
steps.instruction: Find an American beech that is an adult or established juvenile with diameter at breast height (DBH) greater than 10 cm (>4 in). Use a fabric measuring tape or TreeSnap (step 5) to calculate DBH from circumference. If no adult trees are present, a regenerating tree may be used. Verify the tree is American beech (not European beech).

steps.title: Start TreeSnap observation
steps.instruction: Open the TreeSnap app, tap the American Beech button, select “Collection Purpose”, then choose “Adventure Scientists & UConn Beech Leaf Collection”.

steps.title: Collect three healthy leaves
steps.instruction: Locate accessible green leaves with no beech leaf disease (BLD) or the mildest symptoms. Cut three leaves using a knife, shears, or by pinching them off. Immediately photograph the leaves for upload to TreeSnap.

steps.title: Package leaves with silica and ID
steps.instruction: Place the three leaves into a tea bag without pulling the strings closed (allow airflow). Label a sample ID card with your name, collection date, latitude and longitude (from TreeSnap). Put the tea bag, silica gel packet, and labeled ID card into a zip‑lock bag, then zip closed without forcing out all air so the silica can absorb moisture.

steps.title: Photograph packaged sample
steps.instruction: Take a picture of the closed zip‑lock bag showing the sample ID card; upload this image to TreeSnap as the “Collection: Photo of Collection Bag”.

steps.title: Complete TreeSnap metadata
steps.instruction: Enter all required fields in the observation, setting the “AS” or “Adventure Scientists” field to “0”. Add the leaf photo and the bag photo. In the Comments field note any observations such as potential disease‑resistant traits, presence of beech leaf‑mining weevil (BLMW), or beech scale collection. Save the entry.

substeps.instruction: If cellular reception is unavailable, tap “Save” → “Upload Later”. When back online, open the app and select the yellow pop‑up to upload the data.

steps.title: Decontaminate tools and shoes
steps.instruction: Clean your shoes and cutting shears with alcohol or bleach before moving to the next tree to prevent spread of BLD.

steps.title: Proceed to next tree
steps.instruction: Select the next tree at least 8 km (5 mi) away and repeat steps 3‑8.

steps.title: Store and monitor samples
steps.instruction: Keep completed zip‑lock bags in a cool, dry place. Periodically check silica gel color; if it changes from orange to mostly green, reactivate the silica.

steps.title: Reactivate silica if needed
steps.instruction: Place the silica packet in an oven for 0.5–2.0 hours at 200–250 °F (do not exceed 250 °F) or microwave on DEFROST for about 5–8 minutes. Avoid high‑power settings that may melt the packet. Allow the packet to cool before returning it to the zip‑lock bag.

steps.title: Mail samples and notify
steps.instruction:
When all collections are finished, place the zip‑lock bags into the reusable mailer, include the APHIS Letter of No Permit for Canadian shipments, tape the mailer closed, and send to:
